prompt: Implement reservoir sampling: pick one item uniformly at random from a list in a single pass, using rng.nextInt(i + 1) at each index. Complete the sampleOne and sampleMany methods in the starter file.
explanation: Reservoir sampling keeps one candidate and replaces it at index i with probability 1/(i+1), which is exactly what rng.nextInt(i + 1) == 0 tests. The arithmetic works out so that after the whole pass every item has an equal 1/n chance of being the survivor, even though the algorithm never needed to know n in advance. Handling null and empty input before the loop keeps the loop itself free of special cases.
hints: Handle the null or empty list before you create the Random -- return null straight away.
At index i call rng.nextInt(i + 1); a result of 0 means the new item replaces the kept one. Index 0 always wins because nextInt(1) can only return 0.
sampleMany just loops: trial t calls sampleOne(items, seed + t) and adds the result to a list.
